title: Start Making And Keep The Process
objective: Begin the pupil’s new print-and-collage artwork using taught overlap and joining steps, and preserve an actual making stage with the pupil’s own choice.

blocks.text: Explore · Part C · Create. Start making and keep the process.
Today you will turn your loose idea into the start of your artwork. Learn how to place and join dry paper, then keep a clear record of what you made.
We are making a new print and collage. A print is a mark pressed from one surface to another. A collage joins pieces to make one image.
Bring forward the tests and idea from C1. Keep them beside today’s work so a reader can follow your steps. The final artwork will join this record when it is finished.
You can point, speak, type or write to show your choices. You may make a pattern or a made-up place. Your art does not have to tell a story about your life.

This deck supports Explore Part C, Create. Part C requires an artwork, a record of the PROCESS, and the final work. The new print-and-collage activity is distinct from the drawing and paper sculpture in Part A and the live or active exploration in Part B. Do not relabel a finished A or B work as C. Source: tools/artsaward/SPEC.json, Explore and universal rules. Mark each part P / A / N. Overall Pass allows ONE Attempted. Any Not Attempted = Below Pass. Results are Pass or Below Pass only. The whole Explore digital portfolio has a 10-file cap. Organise it by part; four cumulative files, Explore-A, Explore-B, Explore-C and Explore-D, are a suggested arrangement, not one new file per lesson. Every evidence locator must name the actual file plus page, slide or timecode. The three assessment areas are art form knowledge and understanding, creativity, and communication. Core, Extend and Challenge vary support within Explore; each retains the pupil’s own artwork, process record and final work across C1–C4. Only an adviser trained at Explore may assess. Delivery is through a validated centre; staff must confirm these conditions, which this deck does not assert are met. Adults may scribe the pupil’s exact words and check them back. They must not write plans, reviews or evidence for the pupil. Staff may record factual observations of access support separately. No visit, booking, meeting or date is asserted. Keep the theme on art choices; no private life account is required.

Explore Part C C2 continues the new print-and-collage activity begun in C1. Retrieve each pupil’s real C1 records and dry print samples. If that start is absent, allow a fresh test and pupil choice before making; do not supply a completed adult plan. Prepare backing card, glue sticks, scrap mats, safe scissors, pre-cut shapes and dry texture paper. Check access and local handling rules. Provide a camera or a means to retain samples and short accounts. Record image credits. Preserve the loose layout before fixing it. An adult may steady materials or operate an access aid at the pupil’s direction, but must not make the creative choices. No completed stage is asserted before it has happened.

stages.title: Arrival · retrieve

blocks.text: Find the idea and test you kept last time. Point to the print or paper you chose. What did you want the marks or gaps to do in your image?
Check the paint is dry before you touch or glue the paper. Lay the prints beside your fresh backing card. Keep your tests safe; they show how you reached this point.
You can keep your first idea or change it. If it changes, save the old sketch first and say what you now want to try. A real change belongs in your making record.

stages.data-ta1: Check that pupils are using their own new Part C work. Retrieve the start record without replacing it. Help pupils locate it rather than invent a reason for a missing choice.

stages.title: Starter · create the need

blocks.text: Look at two loose shapes on the board. One sits beside the other. Now one moves partly over the other. Which shape seems to be in front? Point to the edge that helps you tell.
Where we place a piece changes the image. A big gap may split the page. An overlap may link two parts. We can move loose pieces to try these effects before we glue.
What could go wrong if we glue at once? We may hide a mark we meant to show. We may fill a space we meant to leave clear.
Today we will test the layout, save that state, then join the pieces. Glue is a making step, not a race to cover the card.

stages.data-ta1: Use two large real shapes so pupils can track the moved edge. Describe front and behind aloud. Accept different preferences while checking what the overlap physically hides.

stages.title: I Do · model

blocks.text: Watch me use dry prints to start a fresh collage. I tear around one printed shape. I turn the paper as I tear so my hands can follow the edge. A rough edge can be part of my choice.
I put the large piece down first. Then I place a small piece partly across it. I leave the print I like in view. I move the small piece back and compare the gap.
Before I fix anything, I save a view of this loose layout. I make a small sketch as another way to keep it. The sketch shows where the two pieces meet.
I lift one piece and turn it over on a scrap mat. I spread a thin coat of glue across the back, close to its edges. I place it back, hold the card still, and press from the middle out.

blocks.title: Keep the layout before the join
blocks.caption: Save the loose stage before you fix it to the card.
blocks.alt: PLACE: try a loose layout. SAVE: keep its first state. GLUE: coat the paper back. PRESS: work from the centre. Save the loose stage before you fix it to the card.

blocks.text: I lift a corner gently to check the join. If it rises, I add a little glue there and press again. I keep glue away from the print surface.

stages.data-ta1: Demonstrate tearing or accessible cutting, overlap, a real before-state record and a thin glue coat. Preserve the model record. Follow product instructions and local drying arrangements.

stages.title: We Do · everyone commits

data.heading: Keep the step before it is hidden
data.instruction: Order this four-step collage join. Use each position once. Then say why the loose layout is kept before glue is used.

items.label: Press the piece down, then check the dry edge.
items.feedback: Press gently. Once the join is ready, check for a loose corner.

items.label: Try the dry pieces and choose their overlap.
items.feedback: A loose trial lets you move shapes before they are fixed.

items.label: Put a thin coat of glue on the chosen piece.
items.feedback: Add glue after you have kept a record of the chosen loose layout.

items.label: Keep a sketch or image of the loose layout.
items.feedback: This saves a real making stage that the join will change.

data.discussion: Try the join on scraps. Ask before touching someone else’s work. A helper can steady the card; the layout choice stays yours.

stages.data-ta1: Collect an answer from each pupil before revealing the key. The visible cards can be sorted by number with no extra pack. Re-model glue use if the join sequence is unclear.

stages.title: I Do 2 · connect

blocks.text: My work sample and my words do different jobs. The sample shows the torn edge and the overlap. My words explain the choice I made.

blocks.title: Show the step and name the choice

boxes.head: MY CHOICE
boxes.line2: to show more of the print

blocks.caption: Keep what happened with your own words about it.
blocks.alt: MAKING STAGE: loose layout kept, print edge still in view. MY CHOICE: I moved the top piece, to show more of the print. Keep what happened with your own words about it.

blocks.text: I compare my loose sketch with the fixed start. I can point to the same two shapes in each. A reader can see how the work grew.
I add a short note: I moved the small piece to show more of the print. That is what I did in the model. Your note should name a step you took in your own work.
If I need help to hold the backing, I can still choose where each piece goes. Help with a grip does not give someone else the right to choose my image.

stages.data-ta1: Model an accurate connection between an actual image and a spoken or written account. Record access support factually and separately; never turn it into a pupil-authored claim.

stages.title: We Do 2 · lab

blocks.text: Use two dry scraps to practise a join before working on your main piece. Place them with an overlap. Turn one over, add a thin glue coat and press it into place.
Check the edge with an adult or partner when it is ready. Does it lie flat? What would help a loose corner? Add glue only where it is needed.
Keep this small test or a clear image of it. Say what the test taught you about the join. Now look at where that skill could help on your own card.

stages.data-ta1: Provide a dry sample if drying takes longer than the stage. Pupils preserve their real test; do not label a still-wet join as tested dry. Allow an access aid or ready-cut scraps.

stages.title: Independent · evidence

blocks.text: Set out the first part of your own collage. Move the loose pieces until the shapes and gaps suit your idea. Save this layout before you glue it.
Join a section using the steps you have practised. Keep the edge of a print you want people to see. Stop to look at how the new join affects the image.

items: Core: use large dry pieces, an easy-grip glue stick and a helper to steady the card. Choose the layout yourself. Keep a process sample and your own words; retain the final artwork when ready.
Extend: place and join your chosen pieces, keeping a record before and after the join. Add your own choice note. Keep these process records and the final artwork.
Challenge: compare two overlaps before fixing one. Say how your choice changes the image. Keep both layout trials, your process record and the final artwork.

blocks.text: Record a real step today. A picture of the finished adult model is not a record of your making. Your work can be at an early stage and still show a clear choice.

stages.data-ta1: Check for real making and a preserved stage in each route. Scribe only the pupil’s exact words and check them back. Time needed for safe making or drying may continue in recorded programme time.

stages.title: Exit · check the trail

blocks.text: Set the work in its safe drying place. Keep the loose-layout record, join test and new work state together. Do not throw away the early test when the join works.
Add the record to your existing Explore-C file. Give its actual file name and page or slide. For a recording, give the file name and timecode. Credit the person who took each image.
Point to a step you made today and one part to work on next. Your trail has begun to show the process. It will also hold the final artwork when you finish it.

stages.data-ta1: Check the locator against the actual file. Retain labelled originals if saving is pending. Record unfinished or wet work honestly and arrange the next making opportunity.

print.intro: Start your new collage from your own idea. Try and save a loose layout, then join a section and record what you chose.

tiers: Core: choose the layout with large pieces and access help. Keep a process sample, your own words and the final work when ready.
Extend: keep before and after records of your own join and choice. Retain the process and final work.
Challenge: compare overlaps, then join your choice. Keep both trials, the process and final work.
checks: I am making my own new Part C artwork.
I saved the loose layout before fixing it.
A real sample or image shows a step I took.
My process trail will include the final artwork when it is ready.
The evidence has an actual file name and page, slide or timecode.
